chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, this knowledge has a lock upon it, and its key is asking [questions].'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.الْعِلْم: Knowledge — here referring to religious/divine knowledge, the teachings of the Imams
key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَة: Asking/questioning — the act of posing questions to scholars to access knowledge
key_terms.قُفْل: Lock — metaphor for knowledge being inaccessible without the right approach

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the key to knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that religious knowledge is like a locked treasure that can only be accessed through the act of asking questions of the scholars. The hadith emphasizes that inquiry and questioning are not merely permitted but are the essential means of unlocking divine knowledge. This teaching appears in the chapter on asking scholars and discussing with them, reflecting the Shia tradition of active intellectual engagement with qualified religious authorities. A second chain through Ali ibn Ibrahim and al-Sakuni confirms the same teaching.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al Qaddah,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘This knowledge, there is a lock upon it and its key is the asking’.
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfal, from Al Sakuny, from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ari from ’Abdallah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “This knowledge (the knowledge of the holy Prophet and Ahlul Bayt(a.s.)) is under a lock and the key to it is asking”
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni from Imam abu ‘Abdallah has narrated the same Hadith.
